stories.title: Dell Launches Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents for Agentic AI
stories.body: Dell is adding three new capabilities to its enterprise AI stack: a Unified Semantic Layer that establishes a common business vocabulary across structured and unstructured data, an Enterprise Knowledge Graph that maps relationships including metadata and lineage, and Knowledge Agents. Dell plans to incorporate NVIDIA's open-source Auto-Ontology technology to help construct knowledge graphs from enterprise data. The architecture is designed to operate within the customer's own environment to address data sovereignty and security, and to avoid locking customers into a specific AI model, data platform, or storage provider.
stories.why: This is a named vendor making a full architecture commitment — semantic layer, knowledge graph, and agents as a bundled on-premises stack — which is exactly the data foundation argument Graas must win before agents can operate reliably. Use it on calls to show that hyperscalers now validate the context-layer-first thesis, and that enterprises without this foundation will buy it from someone.

stories.title: McKinsey Survey: 71% of Retail Merchants Say AI Tools Have Had Limited or No Effect — the Problem Is Integration, Not Technology
stories.body: McKinsey's January 2026 report 'Merchants Unleashed: How Agentic AI Transforms Retail Merchandising' found that while most retail merchandising teams have invested in automation tools and experimented with AI, 71 percent of merchants surveyed said AI merchandising tools have had limited to no effect on their business so far. McKinsey attributes this not to the technology but to how it is integrated and used. The report argues agentic AI changes the dynamic by shifting decision-making from static weekly cycles to continuous, autonomous tuning of assortments, prices, and promotions.
stories.why: This is the single most powerful stat for a Graas salesperson to put in front of a merchant or category management leader — the majority of retail AI investments are stalling, and McKinsey names poor integration, not model quality, as the root cause. It directly validates the argument that a governed context and data layer must come before agents can deliver value.

stories.tag: Global - analyst research / CPG-retail supply chain
stories.title: BCG Publishes Outcome Numbers for Agentic AI in CPG–Retail Supply Chains: +2–4% In-Stocks, 60%+ Planning Productivity Gains
stories.body: A BCG analysis published in 2026 finds that agentic AI can boost in-stocks by 2–4% and planning productivity by over 60% for CPG companies and retailers by enabling synchronized, always-on supply chains. BCG describes agents that continuously monitor store- and DC-level inventory signals against sell-through velocity and proactively generate replenishment recommendations before a retailer's own replenishment cycle would catch the gap. A separate BCG Executive Perspectives paper on supply chains notes that an agentic-enabled supply chain can optimize inventory daily at the most granular level, simultaneously improving effectiveness and efficiency in ways traditional AI tools could not.
stories.why: These are named outcome numbers from a tier-one consultancy covering exactly the CPG-retailer replenishment workflow that retail agents target — not forecasts but reported field results. A seller can cite the 2–4% in-stocks improvement and 60%+ productivity figure to justify an ROI case and to frame Graas as the execution layer that makes these outcomes possible.

stories.title: Sierra Raises $950M at $15.8B Valuation; Passes $200M ARR — Decagon Launches Voice 3 and Personal Agent Gateway in October 2026
stories.body: Sierra raised $950 million at a $15.8 billion valuation in May 2026, led by Tiger Global and GV, and by August 2026 had reportedly surpassed $200 million in annualized recurring revenue. Decagon, Sierra's closest specialist challenger in customer-service AI, raised $250 million at a $4.5 billion valuation in January 2026 and in October 2026 launched Voice 3 — shipping its first proprietary speech model, Chord, from Decagon Labs — along with a Personal Agent Gateway, becoming a launch partner on OpenAI's B2B marketplace. Decagon's June 2026 product roundup cited a named customer outcome: Hunter Douglas generated $1 million in AI-attributed revenue through Decagon, with an 85% higher average order value.
stories.why: Sierra and Decagon are the two agent vendors Graas is most likely to encounter in a retail or CPG enterprise bake-off; knowing Sierra's $150K annual floor, Decagon's lower-floor per-conversation model, and both companies' October 2026 product moves lets a seller anchor commercial and product comparisons precisely. The Hunter Douglas outcome number is the kind of concrete proof point a buyer will table — Graas needs a sharper counter-example ready.

stories.title: Gartner: 40%+ of Agentic AI Projects to Be Canceled by 2027; CIOs Shift AI Buying Authority to Finance as 'Blank-Check Era' Ends
stories.body: Gartner's 2026 forecasts, cited across multiple enterprise IT analyses, project that more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027 due to governance gaps, and describe 2026 as a 'trough of disillusionment' year in which ROI must be proven before anything scales. Gartner also expects AI to reach enterprises primarily as embedded features from incumbent software providers rather than as new greenfield builds, putting pressure on pure point-solution vendors. McKinsey's 2026 survey separately found that 32% of enterprise respondents decided against buying at least one software product because they believed they could build it in-house with agentic coding tools — a trend concentrated in technology and healthcare sectors.
stories.why: Every enterprise retail prospect will be under pressure to justify AI spend before year-end; the 40%-cancellation forecast arms a seller with urgency and a governance argument — pilots stall not because agents fail technically but because the data and context foundation was never put in place. The build-vs-buy tension is a live procurement objection: Gartner's data showing vendor-led projects succeed twice as often as pure in-house builds (67% vs 33%) closes the conversation.
